column3: NASB renders “puffs up” as “makes arrogant” and “builds up” as “edifies.”
NASB follows the critical text without “nothing”; “thinks to have known” is rendered “supposes that he knows.”
NASB renders “he has known by Him” as “he is known by Him.”
NASB follows the critical text without “other”; it renders “an idol is nothing” as “there is no such thing as an idol.”
NASB renders “of whom” as “from whom” and adds “exist.”
NASB follows the critical text (“accustomed”); it adds “food” and “it were.”
NASB follows the critical text; “come short” is rendered “the worse,” and “have an advantage” is “the better.”
NASB follows the critical text; “right” is rendered “liberty.”
NASB follows the critical text; “is destroyed” is rendered “is ruined.”
NASB renders “snares” as “causes … to stumble” and “to the age” as “never … again.”
